Getting started

...Thunder has four screens: the Synth, where you build an 8-pad kit; the Tracker, a sequencer that plays that kit; …waves, a modular synth that plays as a layer oscillator; and …chains, where you design modular effects chains for the tracker’s tracks (Mixer → CHN). Switch at the top. ⚙ Settings → App → Mobile turns the app into ...Thunder for phones: Synth and Tracker only, with PAD input. …waves layers and …chains effects still play there, so the same files work in both. Everything saves in the browser as you work; File ▾ saves a project file (song and kit) you can keep or move to another device, and opens, renders and exports. There is also a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux (github.com/matthettich/thunder-plus/releases/latest) that keeps itself up to date; it keeps its own songs and kits, so use File to move work between it and the browser.

How a song fits together

Song (256 rows × 16 tracks of sect numbers) → Sect (up to 16 phrases, each with a transpose) → Phrase (up to 32 rows of note, volume, instrument and three effects) → Inst (which pad a note plays, with transpose, volume, pan, reverse and start). Mixer, FX and Project sit around them.

Starting a new song resets the pattern numbering to 00. Project → › NEW SONG (EDIT×2) or › LOAD DEMO begins with its first block at 00; the numbers never carry over from the previous song.

Sects are hidden by default (⚙ Settings → Hide sect page, or Project → SECT): EDIT×2 on an empty song cell makes a block that already holds a phrase, SHIFT+▶ opens that phrase, and EDIT×2 on a filled block makes a unique copy. Set SECT to SHOWN for the sect screen; nothing is lost either way.

PLAY in Song starts from the block under the cursor, or from the top when the cell under the cursor is empty.

Arrange (wide screens): the overview at the right shows the whole song, lined up with the Song screen (scroll either one and the other follows). A tap on a block goes to it (a second tap opens its phrase). Holding a block mutes or unmutes just that one — the phrase stays in place, silent, so you can drop parts in and out while arranging. Tap a row number to play from there; in KEYS mode M mutes the block under the Song cursor. Whole tracks are muted in the Mixer, never here, so a slip can’t silence a track.

The screens are laid out as a map: Song ▶ Sect ▶ Phrase ▶ Inst left to right, Project above, Mixer below, FX to the right of the Mixer. You move between them with the screen keys below, the tabs, or the map in the side panel.

Pluck string

A layer type (Layer → Type → Pluck string): a Karplus–Strong plucked string. A burst of noise rings round a delay one period long, losing its top end as it goes, so it sounds like a guitar, harp or koto string. Bright sets the pluck and how fast the highs fade; Decay how long it rings. Give the layer's Amp a long decay (or sustain) so the string can ring out. In …waves the String module is the same string with a Gate to pluck it, a pick Position and a Mute for when the note ends.

Blip engine

Synth → Engine: Blip (any pad, drums too) turns a pad into a minimal electronic drum, in the spirit of the generative blip grooveboxes: a parabolic tone with a Kick (a fast pitch drop; Kick time sets how fast), FM (and its ratio), Ring mod (slow is a tremolo, fast is metal), Noise and Click, then Decay, Drive, a Filter (left of centre low-pass, right high-pass) and Grain (the hit repeated, each quieter: a stutter). Presets go from Click and Boom to Metal, Tick hat and Glitch; Random rolls a new one. In …chains and …waves, the Blip drum module plays eight of these voices and the Life module sequences them.

Voice engine

Synth → Engine: Voice turns a synth slot (9–16) into a singing robot. Type the lyrics: each note the tracker plays sings the next syllable (its consonants on the attack, the vowel held until the note ends), and PLAY starts the lyrics again from the top. A slide keeps the syllable it's on, for runs over one vowel. The chips under the lyrics show every syllable as the engine will say it. If a word comes out wrong, split it with a hyphen (to-night) or spell it in brackets with ARPAbet sounds: [HH EH L OW] (AA AE AH AO AW AY EH ER EY IH IY OW OY UH UW AX; B CH D DH F G HH JH K L M N NG P R S SH T TH V W Y Z ZH). Robot goes from a natural voice to a buzzy one, Size changes the voice's size (bigger is deeper), Voice at 0 whispers, Diction speeds the consonants up or slows them down. A full stop, comma, ; : ! ? or _ is a rest: that note (or pad step) is silent, so hello . world pauses between the words and several in a row pause longer. Consonant noise sets how loud the hiss of K, T, P, S and H is, and Clarity narrows the formants and lifts their presence so words are easier to make out. The pad (and exports) sing the whole line, one syllable every Pad step. One voice per track (mono).

Bass engine

Any synth slot (08 and up) can be a bass instead of layers: on the Synth page pick Engine: Bass. It is an additive mono bass in the spirit of Reaktor's Lazerbass, for dubstep and drum & bass: up to 64 partials (Shape goes saw › square › triangle; Bright, Odd / even, Stretch), a sub oscillator, a resonant low-pass with its own envelope, vowel formants, a comb, Reese detune and stereo Width. The Wobble moves the cutoff, vowel, comb and level at a rate locked to the song's tempo (4 bars down to 1/32, triplets and dotted). In the tracker it plays live, so the wobble keeps time on every note however high you play, a held note wobbles for as long as it's held, and Glide and Legato slide between notes (PSL slides without restarting). The WOB command changes the rate from a row on (WOB 06 = 1/4, WOB 0B = 1/16, WOB 00 back to the voice's own). Presets get you started; the bottom panel's instrument section shows its level, cutoff, resonance and wobble. The voice's Level, Tune and Drive apply; pad effects don't (use the track's FX).

Mastering

Settings → Master → Open mastering… (or the MASTERING cell on the Mixer's master row: ▶ from the master level, then EDIT; or › MASTERING on the FX screen's master) puts a chain on the master bus: EQ → Suppress → Compress → Limit. Each has its own switch; the readouts show short-term loudness in and out (LUFS) and the highest peak. EQ: drag a point (left/right is frequency, up/down is gain), shift-drag or scroll for width, double-click empty space to add a bell, double-click a point to switch it off; the band row sets exact values. Suppress turns down resonances that stick out of the spectrum (Depth, Sharpness, Selectivity, Speed; drag the lines to set its range; Delta plays only what it removes). Compress is a glue compressor (its sidechain high-pass keeps the bass from pumping it). Limit catches every peak at the Ceiling, between samples too. Renders of the song include the chain and keep its ceiling; stems don't.

Settings

⚙ Settings at the top: it starts with Audio (output device, level, latency, rate), then this screen’s own settings (in the tracker every Project setting: Song, Input, Screen, Render), then Master, Skin, Export, MIDI, Kit and App (Mobile, install, check for update). There you can also turn off Display steps as decimal (row numbers in hex), turn off Play note on entry (audition notes as you type them), show or hide the KEYS-mode on-screen keypad (Settings → KEYS KEYPAD; it starts hidden on a computer and shown in the Mobile setup), and change the Text size of the tracker screen. With the KEYS keypad off, a bottom panel takes its place: a spectrum of the master, quick controls for the current instrument’s sound and the current track’s effects, and a channel strip for the current track (stereo meter, fader with 0 dB at E0 and +6 dB at the top, pan, M and S). Tap a section’s button to hide it (it waits as a dashed + button); drag the panel’s top edge for its height and the scope’s or FX section’s edge for their widths. On a big screen the space beside the grid is the stage (Settings → STAGE): BY SCREEN shows something useful for each screen (the dogs dance to the beat on Song and Project, Sect previews the phrase, Phrase shows a piano lighting the notes as they play, Inst the waveform, Mixer the master spectrum, FX the effects chain), DOGS shows the dogs everywhere, OFF leaves it empty. In the bar above the grid, double-click the tempo or LPB to type a new one (ticks a step are in Settings). The panel follows the track the cursor is on: its instrument (on Song, the one the block under the cursor plays), its effects and its strip. When any track is soloed, SOLO · CLEAR shows; ✕ hides the panel and Settings → BOTTOM PANEL brings it back. Drag a finger up or down anywhere on the tracker screen to scroll; drag on the cursor's cell to change its value.

Drum pads and synths

The kit has 16 slots. 1–8 are drum pads: one-shots that play their whole sound. 9–16 are synths for melodies and chords (Bass, Pluck, Keys, Pad, Lead, Bell, Organ, Sub to start): a note holds at its sustain level for as long as you hold it, up to the slot’s Max len, then fades over its release when you let go. C-4 plays middle C. In the tracker, instruments 08–0F play the synth slots in a new song. A voice per track (Settings → Kit) grows the kit past 16 slots: every song track gets its own pad — drums on mono tracks, a simple synth on poly ones. The pads stay the same size and scroll up and down.

Chopping breaks

Load a drum loop into a pad (Synth → Load sample), then on its instrument (INST) set SLICES (GRID cuts equal parts, HITS cuts at each drum hit it finds). Each note now plays one slice: C-4 the first, C#4 the second and so on, so you can rearrange the break in a phrase. SYNC fits the loop to the song tempo: set BEATS to how long the loop is (or use › GUESS BEATS). REPITCH changes its speed and pitch together; STRETCH keeps the pitch with smooth grains; LOOP keeps the pitch with little tempo-synced loops for a gritty, stuttery sound (GRAIN sets their length). › PLAY SLICES auditions them in order.

Chords and polyphony

The second half of the tracks is polyphonic (9–16 with 16 tracks, 17–32 with 32; Settings → Song → Tracks): the green POLY box on the right of Song and Mixer. The first half, in the pink MONO box on the left, plays one note at a time. Open a phrase from a polyphonic track and it shows four note columns, N1–N4, so a row can hold a chord. Notes on these tracks ring over each other, up to 4 at a time per track; a fifth steals the oldest. A note OFF in any note column releases everything on the track. The mono tracks stay one note at a time, and a phrase played there uses only N1.

Two input modes

PAD is a d-pad plus SHIFT, PLAY, OPTION and EDIT, good with a thumb. KEYS is direct entry: type notes, hex and effects, with an on-screen keypad on touch screens. The keyboard works in both — in PAD mode Z and X stay OPTION and EDIT and Alt+arrows page; everything else types as in KEYS. Switch with ⚙ Settings → Input (or Project → INPUT).

One finger is enough. With Sticky keys on, tap SHIFT or OPTION alone and it stays lit for the next button. The command row (Project → COMMANDS) gives every two-key command its own button: change, prev/next, clear, select, copy, cut, paste, play song, and on the SONG screen CLN↓ (clones the block, or the selected blocks, into new numbers on the row below) and CLN (clone): the block under the cursor is copied, phrases and all, to the next free number.

On a computer keyboard in PAD mode the keyboard is not disabled: arrows move, Enter opens, Space plays, typing letters and hex edits the cell, and Shift selects lines. Z stays OPTION (not a note), X stays EDIT, and Alt+arrows page (OPTION+arrow) rather than change the value.

Touch

Tap a cell to move there; tap it again to open or add. Drag up or down on the cursor’s cell to change its value; drag elsewhere to scroll.

Track effects

Each track and the master have 4 effect slots (FX screen, or the Mixer’s FX row): 34 effects in all: EQ, compressor, three reverbs, tape delay, dub tape, saturation, drive, tube, tape, vinyl, lo-fi, bitcrush, chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo, trance gate, auto-wah, ladder filter, comb resonator, wavefolder, overdrive, pitch and frequency shifters, cross-mod, transient shaper, multiband squash, speaker cab, air, and Rings, Clouds and Beads. On the Mixer’s FX row, OPTION (Alt in KEYS mode) + ▲▶ turns a track's effects on in order, up to four, and OPTION + ▼◀ turns the last one off without losing its settings — turn the count back up and it returns; with none on, slots fill from 1. EDIT on the row opens the FX screen. Renders include them; stems skip the master effects and limiter.

The FX screen keeps the slot list and the open slot's controls apart: ▲▼ move within one of the two, and ◀▶ (or a sideways swipe) open the slot under the cursor and go back to the list — so scrolling never changes the effect you are editing. A filled slot shows ›, and the open one shows ▪.

…chains (the modular effects screen) is live: adding or removing a module, moving a cable, or turning a slider is heard at once — no need to restart playback. Its Resample module records what passes through it into a pad, starting on the next bar, and slices it so you can chop it like a breakbeat.

Synth page

Z–/ · Q–PPlay the selected pad chromatically; C-4 is its own pitch. On a synth slot (9–16) notes hold while the keys are down, so you can play chords
− =Octave down / up
Shift 1–8 or ◀ ▶Pick a pad (◀▶ go through all 16 slots)
SpacePlay the pad as it is
Alt 1–7Jump into a tracker screen

Presets: the list beside the pad name loads a whole sound (kicks, snares, hats, percussion, IDM and glitch hits, basses, pads, chords, keys and leads, including Bass and Blip engine sounds). ＋ Save this as a preset… keeps the pad in this song's own list, at the top; it travels in the project file. The Layer presets list in the layer card swaps just the selected layer (a snare's noise, a clicky pitch sweep…) and keeps it at the right pitch on any pad. File ▾ → Export song presets… / Import presets… moves them between songs and devices; Save kit / Load kit moves all 16 pads at once.

Voice pitch, filter & amp (in the card under the pad name) shape the whole voice at once, across every layer: a pitch envelope, a low-pass filter with its own envelope, and an amp envelope. Each envelope has an Amount slider setting how far it is applied. The layer card's Filter and Amp sections still shape only the selected layer.

Mod matrix (Voice card): 3 LFOs (rate, shape, depth), 3 envelopes (A/D/S/R) and a 32-step sequencer, each routed to one destination — pitch, level, low-pass cutoff or high-pass cutoff — with a signed amount, applied across all of the voice's layers. Every amount starts at zero. Turn it up and sweep a filter, wobble the pitch, or shape the level. Mod envelopes has a Reset to defaults button that puts the pitch, amp and the three mod envelopes back to their factory values.

Voice play: Glide slides the pitch from the last note; Mono + Legato retunes the sounding note instead of retriggering. Tuning (song) is a cents offset per pitch class (Equal, Just, Pythagorean and Meantone presets or your own), applied to live playing and the tracker. The Wavetable oscillator (Position/Formant) and its Bend/Unison/Spread/Sub/Noise sit in the layer card when that type is picked.

Engine (synth slots): Layers is the layer synth above; Bass swaps in the bass engine and Voice a singing voice that sings typed lyrics, and Blip (on any pad) a minimal electronic drum (see Bass, Voice and Blip engine on the Start tab). Acid is a mono bass-line synth (saw or square into a squelchy ladder filter): a note with a volume of C0 or more is accented, and PSL slides. Machine is a mono synth with seven machines (Dual VCO, Chip, FM+, Swarm, Ensemble, Noise, Additive), each with its own A, B and C, then high- and low-pass filters, an amp envelope and an LFO. Both play live in the tracker. Tone drum is a modelled drum (a tone with a pitch bend or an inharmonic spectrum, filtered noise with a sweep, a click, distortion), and Modal a struck, plucked, bowed or blown object (bar, marimba, vibes, glock, bell, gong, membrane, glass, string, tube, wood, plate). On a poly track (9–16) a Voice pad sings chords: notes that start together sing the same syllable in harmony. In ⚙ Settings, Kit saves and loads kits, Export writes WAVs for Koala and SunVox, MIDI connects a controller (notes not mapped to a pad play the selected synth slot, held until note-off) and Skin changes the look (Pastel, Minimal, Neon, Matrix and the Simple colour pairs).

Files and rendering

File ▾ holds Save, Save As and Open, plus Render song (a stereo WAV, through the mastering chain when it is on) and Render stems (a zip with the mix and one WAV per track, without mastering), plus New song, Load demo song, kit save and load, and sharing. In desktop Chrome and Edge, Save writes straight back to the file you opened or last saved; other browsers download a copy, and Save As asks for a name first. The song also saves itself in the browser as you work.

More detail in the README on GitHub.
